items.quote: Service accounts are the recommended method to manage authentication to the Atlas Administration API.
items.why: Says service accounts recommended for auth; claim lists both oauth2 and api_key.

items.quote: API keys are a legacy method of authenticating to the Atlas Administration API that uses HTTP Digest Authentication.
items.why: Says API keys are legacy Digest auth; supports api_key part only, not full claim.

items.quote: Service accounts provide improved security over API (Application Programming Interface) keys by using the industry standard OAuth 2.0 protocol with the Client Credentials flow.
items.why: States service accounts use OAuth 2.0 client credentials; covers oauth2 only.

items.quote: You can create a service account in MongoDB Atlas and use its credentials for authentication.
items.why: Says you can create a service account and use its credentials; no free-tier or signup claim.

items.quote: The Atlas Administration API doesn't provide access to the data stored in your clusters.
items.why: States Admin API lacks cluster data access; no REST, versioning, or breadth details.

items.quote: Many Atlas Administration API endpoint URLs (Uniform Resource Locators) follow the format of `/api/atlas/<version>/groups/<GROUP-ID>/`, where `<GROUP-ID>` is your project ID.
items.why: Shows /api/atlas/<version>/groups URL format; no v2, Accept header, or breadth coverage.

items.quote: A Model Context Protocol server to connect to MongoDB databases and MongoDB Atlas Clusters.
items.why: Describes an MCP server for MongoDB and Atlas; does not say vendor-official or give the URL.
